display.purpose: Tea names (italic), about headline, section headings. Always Cormorant Garamond.

title.purpose: Shop name in header. One instance on the page.

body.purpose: All prose: about copy, brewing steps text, footer body. IBM Plex Mono.

label.purpose: Nav links, table headers, section labels, footer headings. Uppercase, wide tracking. IBM Plex Mono.

tea-name.purpose: Tea names in menu table — italic, medium size, Cormorant Garamond.

motion.name: rule-draw
motion.purpose: The site's single animation. Fires once on page load — a 1px horizontal rule draws left-to-right across the header. Represents steeping. Nothing else moves.

breakpoints.name: mobile
breakpoints.note: Spine hides, header stacks, table collapses to stacked block layout

breakpoints.name: tablet
breakpoints.note: About and brewing grids collapse from 2-column to 1-column

components.name: Nav Link

components.name: Brewing Step
components.description: Numbered brewing instruction with amber Cormorant counter and mono body.

narrative.overview:
This system is built on the premise that specificity is the luxury. Not a heritage brand telling you it's special — an actual letter from the farm, typed on a manual, with ink that bled a little at the edges. The estate name, the cultivar, the exact steep time: these are not decoration. They are the product.

The aesthetic is restrained to the point of severity, but warmth enters through specificity of language and the acute contrast of Cormorant Garamond's hairline serifs against IBM Plex Mono's precision spacing. The parchment background is the physical colour of the document the metaphor demands. The ink carries a green undertone — the colour of tea itself.

This system explicitly rejects: mass-market tea aesthetics (T2, glossy gift packaging), bubble-tea-chain branding (casual, quick-service, trend-driven), and the generic warm-artisan template (script fonts, cream backgrounds, stock photography of tea leaves).
keyCharacteristics: Zero border-radius across every surface — sharp edges only
No shadows, no elevation — depth through colour contrast and 1px rules alone
One animation per session load; stillness thereafter
Cormorant Garamond italic for named items; IBM Plex Mono for all data, labels, body
Amber used precisely: brewing step counters and nav hover only

rules.name: The One Amber Rule
rules.body: Amber (#c4751a) appears in exactly two contexts: brewing step counters and nav hover. Nowhere else. Its scarcity is the point.

rules.name: The No-Shadow Rule
rules.body: No box-shadow, filter: drop-shadow, or text-shadow anywhere. Surfaces are separated by 1px rules and colour contrast only.

rules.name: The Flat-By-Default Rule
rules.body: If a design proposal introduces a box-shadow, replace it with a border, a background tint, or a colour change.

rules.name: The Italic-for-Names Rule
rules.body: Cormorant Garamond italic is used exclusively for named things: tea names, headings, the menu footnote, the brewing intro. Running text is never italic.

rules.name: The Mono-for-Data Rule
rules.body: Any piece of information that could appear in a table, label, or measurement uses IBM Plex Mono. Cormorant Garamond never carries factual data.

dos: Do use Cormorant Garamond italic for tea names, headings, and named items only
Do use IBM Plex Mono for all labels, data, measurements, and body text
Do keep amber to brewing step counters and nav hover only
Do use 1px rules as the sole separation mechanism
Do write copy that is specific and named: estate names, cultivar details, steep temperatures
donts: Don't add box-shadow, drop-shadow, or text-shadow to anything
Don't use border-radius anywhere — all corners are sharp
Don't use amber for emphasis outside the two defined contexts
Don't use gradient text or background-clip: text
Don't introduce a new font family — Cormorant Garamond and IBM Plex Mono only
Don't add a second animation — the rule-draw is the site's one deliberate motion moment
Don't use the words premium, artisan, curated, craft, or experience in copy
Don't render the menu as cards — it is a table because it IS a table
